components.name: Hub Deck
components.description: One subject as a deck of dyed card stock.

narrative.overview: Every subject is a 단어장 deck of dyed card stock on a steel ring, and every problem is a white card on that ring. The candidate reads the card, works it out by hand, flips it down from the ring to see the back, and grades it with a red ballpoint: a circle for right, a cross for wrong. The system is an Operate surface first; colour lives in the covers and the four subject dyes, never in chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Card stock, rings and punched holes are the structure, not decoration.
Four subject dyes plus one exam cobalt; grading red is the only other hue.
Korean-first typography with keep-all line breaking.
One signature motion: the answer face swings down from the ring hinge.

rules.name: The Four Dyes Rule
rules.body: Subject colour comes only from the four stock dyes and exam cobalt, assigned by subject group. Never add a per-subject hue.

rules.name: The Red Pen Rule
rules.body: Grading red means graded or answer. Do not use it for decoration, links or errors unrelated to grading.

rules.name: The Keep-All Rule
rules.body: Korean text uses word-break: keep-all; never let a word split mid-syllable-block.

rules.name: The Pen Is Rare Rule
rules.body: The pen face appears only for 정답 and 함정 labels. It never sets sentences.

rules.name: The Stack Only Rule
rules.body: Offset, zero-blur layers are allowed only to draw the cards under a cover. Nowhere else.

dos: Do take subject colour from the group dye (see The Four Dyes Rule).
Do keep answers in the code face inside the red-outlined 정답 box, preserving line breaks for multi-line output.
Do give every new card-like surface the punched hole, and every deck cover the ring.
Do provide a dark-mode value for every new token; dark mode is a night desk, not an inverted page.
donts: Don't add gamification (points, streaks, badges); grading is a private red-pen mark.
Don't use colored left borders thicker than 1px on steps, notes or callouts.
Don't use gradient text, glass panels or eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't introduce a sixth dye or a second accent hue.
